correctness.rationale: Root-stabilizer automorphisms preserve clique-vs-cycle Cartesian directions by triangle counts for m>=3 and square counts for m=2, giving exactly A_d=(cycle distance d, clique coordinate 0), B_d=(distance d, remaining clique coords), d=0..floor(n/2). At refinement round t, the root-colour induced signatures determine rooted walk counts w_0..w_t by induction. A_k and B_(k-1) are the only competing orbit types at root distance k; their shortest-walk counts differ (k versus one, or even antipodal two), except the distance-one collision, which splits at t=2 if m>=3 from length-two counts and at t=3 if m=2 (length-three counts 6 vs 7). For n>=6, D>=3 is enough; n=5,m=2 needs t=3. All vertices beyond t hops of a singled-out root in the (m+1)-regular graph have the same color at round t, and B_D versus A_D remain unsplit at t=D-1, proving optimality. Independently rebuilt direct refinement on 65 parameter pairs n=5..17,m=2..6 and confirmed exact orbit cells and stabilization depth; source 392 vertex and 864 quotient finite tests corroborate rather than prove all n,m.
residual_risks: Only one root initially individualized in C_n□K_m, n>=5, m>=2, synchronous 1-WL with old colors retained; result is within-graph orbit recovery, not graph isomorphism identification.
The lower-bound uniform-distance wavefront induction requires graph regularity and the exact initial coloring; arbitrary root markings are excluded.
